22.name: Auto Flight
22.description: Automatic flight control systems including Autopilot, Flight Director, Auto Thrust and Load Alleviation. The Auto Flight system reduces pilot workload during all phases of flight by automating roll, pitch, heading, altitude, speed, and thrust management.

22-00.name: General
22-00.description: The Auto Flight system receives inputs from Air Data Computers, Inertial Reference Systems, Flight Management Systems, and Radio Altimeters. It processes these inputs through Flight Control Computers and sends commands to flight control surfaces and engine thrust levers via autopilot servos and auto throttle actuators.
bite_tests: Perform Auto Flight BITE via MCDU

22-10.name: Autopilot
22-10.description: The Autopilot system controls roll, pitch, heading, altitude, vertical speed, approach, and landing. It uses Flight Control Computers to compute commands sent to autopilot servos which move flight control surfaces. The system supports CAT I, CAT II, and CAT III autoland operations.

22-20.name: Speed-Attitude Correction
22-20.description: Maintains aircraft speed and pitch attitude automatically. Prevents overspeed, stall, and excessive pitch attitudes. Includes pitch trim compensation and Mach speed stabilization.

22-30.name: Auto Throttle
22-30.description: Automatically controls engine thrust to maintain selected speed or thrust mode. Interfaces with FADEC/EEC for thrust management. Supports TOGA, Go-Around, and speed intervention modes.

22-40.name: System Monitor
22-40.description: Monitors health and status of autopilot, flight director, auto thrust, and all associated sensors. Records faults for maintenance retrieval via BITE and central maintenance systems.

22-50.name: Aerodynamic Load Alleviating
22-50.description: Reduces aerodynamic loads on the airframe during turbulence and maneuvering. Automatically commands spoiler and aileron deflections to reduce wing bending moments and gust loads.

23.name: Communications
23.description: Aircraft communication systems enabling voice and data exchange between flight crew, cabin crew, ground stations, and passengers. Includes HF long-range, VHF line-of-sight, SELCAL selective calling, interphone, and passenger address systems.

23-00.name: General
23-00.description: The Communications system provides all voice and data communication capabilities required for safe aircraft operation. It interfaces with the Audio Management Unit for crew headsets, cabin interphone, and radio transmission. All communication radios are controlled via the Radio Management Panel or integrated avionics interface.

23-10.name: HF Communications
23-10.description: High Frequency radio system operating in 2-30 MHz range for long-range voice communication over oceans and remote areas where VHF coverage is unavailable. Uses sky-wave propagation to achieve ranges exceeding 3000 nautical miles.
possible_causes: Coaxial cable break or moisture ingress

23-20.name: VHF Communications
23-20.description: Very High Frequency radio system operating in 118-137 MHz range for short-range line-of-sight voice and data communication. Primary communication system for ATC, company operations, and emergency frequencies including 121.5 MHz guard.

23-30.name: SELCAL (Selective Calling)
23-30.description: Selective Calling system alerts flight crew via audio tone and visual indicator when a ground station is calling their specific aircraft. Eliminates the need for continuous HF radio monitoring during oceanic operations.
symptoms: SELCAL not responding to ground call
corrective_actions: Test Audio and Visual Alert circuits
preventive_actions: SELCAL code verification during annual check
Alert speaker and indicator functional test

23-40.name: Interphone System
23-40.description: Internal voice communication system enabling conversation between flight crew, cabin crew, and ground maintenance personnel. Includes flight interphone, cabin interphone, and service interphone with dedicated jacks at external panels.

23-50.name: Passenger Address System
23-50.description: Public address system enabling flight crew and cabin crew to make announcements to passengers. Includes prerecorded safety announcements, boarding music, and priority override capability from flight deck.

24.name: Electrical Power
24.description: Generation, distribution, conversion, and storage of AC and DC electrical power. The electrical system powers all avionics, lighting, actuators, and cabin systems. It includes engine-driven generators, APU generator, ground power, transformer rectifiers, and battery backup.

24-00.name: General
24-00.description: The Electrical Power system generates 115V AC at 400Hz via Integrated Drive Generators and converts it to 28V DC via Transformer Rectifier Units. Power distribution is managed by Bus Power Control Units with automatic bus tie and load shedding logic. Battery systems provide emergency backup for essential instruments and APU starting.

24-10.name: Generation
24-10.description: Primary AC power generation via engine-driven Integrated Drive Generators producing 115V AC at 400Hz. The IDG combines a constant speed drive with an AC generator. APU generator provides auxiliary power. Generator Control Units regulate voltage and frequency.
bite_tests: Generator output voltage and frequency test
corrective_actions: Check IDG Oil Level and condition
preventive_actions: IDG oil level check every flight

24-20.name: Distribution
24-20.description: Routes AC and DC power through buses, contactors, and transformers. Includes bus tie logic for power transfer between generators, Transformer Rectifier Units for AC-to-DC conversion, and automatic load shedding during single-generator operation.
possible_causes: Bus tie contactor welded or stuck

24-30.name: Storage (Batteries)
24-30.description: Provides DC power for APU starting, emergency backup of essential instruments, and ground operations without external power. Uses Nickel-Cadmium or Lithium-Ion battery technology with dedicated chargers and temperature monitoring.
corrective_actions: Replace Battery if capacity below limit

24-40.name: External Power
24-40.description: Ground power connection system allowing the aircraft to receive AC power from ground power units while engines are shut down. Includes phase and sequence monitoring to protect aircraft systems from incorrect power supply.

27.name: Flight Controls
27.description: Primary and Secondary Flight Control systems enabling pilot control of aircraft attitude and maneuvering in all three axes: roll (ailerons), pitch (elevators), and yaw (rudder). Secondary controls include high-lift devices (flaps, slats) and speed control (spoilers).

27-00.name: General
27-00.description: Controls aircraft attitude and maneuvering in three axes. Includes Ailerons for roll, Elevators for pitch, Rudder for yaw, Flaps and Slats for lift augmentation, Spoilers for speed control and roll assist, and Horizontal Stabilizer for pitch trim.

27-10.name: Aileron & Tab
27-10.description: Controls aircraft roll movement about the longitudinal axis. Ailerons are located on the trailing edge of each wing. Trim tabs provide hands-off roll trim. Servo actuators provide hydraulic power boost. Position sensors provide feedback to fly-by-wire computers.

27-20.name: Rudder & Tab
27-20.description: Controls aircraft yaw movement about the vertical axis. The rudder also provides engine-out directional control and crosswind landing correction. Yaw damper actuator automatically dampens Dutch roll oscillations.

27-30.name: Elevator & Tab
27-30.description: Controls aircraft pitch movement about the lateral axis. Elevators are located on the horizontal stabilizer trailing edge. Includes elevator trim tabs for hands-off pitch trim and position transducers for fly-by-wire feedback.

27-40.name: Horizontal Stabilizer
27-40.description: Maintains longitudinal stability and provides pitch trim. The Trimmable Horizontal Stabilizer Actuator (THSA) adjusts stabilizer angle to trim the aircraft in pitch. Includes jackscrew mechanism driven by electric or hydraulic motors.

27-50.name: Flaps
27-50.description: High lift devices on wing trailing edge used during takeoff and landing to increase wing area and camber, reducing stall speed. Driven by Power Drive Unit through torque shafts and actuators. Flap asymmetry protection prevents uncommanded movement.

27-60.name: Spoilers, Drag Devices and Variable Aerodynamic Fairings
27-60.description: Spoilers serve multiple functions: roll assist when used differentially, speed brake when deployed symmetrically, and lift dumping on landing. Controlled by Spoiler Control Computers receiving inputs from flight control computers.

27-70.name: Gust Lock & Dampener
27-70.description: Locks flight control surfaces in neutral position when aircraft is parked to prevent wind damage. Dampers reduce control surface oscillations during flight. Gust lock engagement is monitored by cockpit indication.

27-80.name: Lift Augmenting (Slats)
27-80.description: Leading edge slats increase wing camber and area during takeoff and landing, reducing stall speed. Driven by Power Drive Unit through torque shafts and actuators. Slat asymmetry protection prevents uncommanded extension or retraction.

31.name: Indicating / Recording Systems
31.description: Flight data recording, cockpit voice recording, central maintenance monitoring, and data link communication systems. These systems capture and store operational data for accident investigation, maintenance troubleshooting, and airline operations.

31-00.name: General
31-00.description: The Indicating and Recording Systems group encompasses all data acquisition, recording, and maintenance monitoring functions. Flight Data Recorders and Cockpit Voice Recorders are crash-survivable units required by aviation regulations. Central Maintenance Computers collect fault data from all aircraft systems.

31-10.name: Flight Data Recording (FDR)
31-10.description: Records critical flight parameters including altitude, airspeed, heading, vertical acceleration, control surface positions, engine parameters, and system status. Data is stored in crash-survivable memory capable of withstanding 3400g impact, 1100°C fire, and deep ocean immersion.

31-20.name: Cockpit Voice Recording (CVR)
31-20.description: Records cockpit audio including crew conversations, radio transmissions, alarms, and ambient sounds for accident investigation. Records minimum 2 hours of audio in crash-survivable memory with continuous loop recording.

31-30.name: Central Maintenance Computer (CMC)
31-30.description: Collects, processes, and stores fault data from all aircraft systems for maintenance troubleshooting. Interfaces with Line Replaceable Units via ARINC 429/629 buses. Provides maintenance reports, fault isolation, and system test capabilities via MCDU or maintenance terminal.

31-40.name: Data Link (ACARS)
31-40.description: Aircraft Communications Addressing and Reporting System enables digital text-based communication between aircraft and ground stations. Used for ATC clearances, company operations messages, maintenance reports, and position reporting.

34.name: Navigation
34.description: Navigation systems providing position, heading, altitude, and approach guidance. Includes VOR/ILS for precision approach, DME for distance, Radio Altimeter for height above terrain, GPS/ADIRU for primary navigation, and Weather Radar for storm avoidance.

34-00.name: General
34-00.description: The Navigation system provides all position, heading, attitude, and approach reference data required for safe aircraft operation in all weather conditions. Primary navigation is provided by GPS and ADIRU. Approach guidance is provided by ILS. Terrain awareness is enhanced by Radio Altimeter and Weather Radar.

34-10.name: VOR / ILS Navigation
34-10.description: VHF Omnidirectional Range provides bearing information from ground stations. Instrument Landing System provides precision approach guidance with Localizer for lateral alignment and Glideslope for vertical guidance. Marker Beacons indicate distance from runway threshold.

34-20.name: DME (Distance Measuring Equipment)
34-20.description: Measures slant range distance from aircraft to DME ground station by timing interrogation-reply signal pairs. Provides distance information for navigation and approach procedures. Operates in paired channels with VOR or ILS frequencies.

34-30.name: Radio Altimeter
34-30.description: Provides precise height above terrain from 0 to 2500 feet using FM-CW radar principle. Critical for CAT II/III autoland, GPWS/TAWS terrain warning, and approach decision heights. Uses separate transmit and receive antennas mounted on fuselage underside.

34-40.name: GPS / ADIRU
34-40.description: Global Positioning System provides satellite-based position. Air Data Inertial Reference Unit combines Air Data Computer and Inertial Reference System to provide attitude, heading, airspeed, altitude, and position. Primary navigation reference for all flight phases.
possible_causes: GPS antenna damage or cable fault

34-50.name: Weather Radar
34-50.description: Detects weather formations ahead of aircraft for storm avoidance. Uses X-band radar with antenna stabilization to maintain scan plane during aircraft pitch and roll. Displays precipitation intensity in color-coded format on Navigation Display.
